title: Enumerate equilibria of a supplied rational bimatrix game
statement: Given rational m by n payoff matrices with m,n <= 3 and a certified nondegeneracy assumption, reproduce support enumeration and output every Nash equilibrium with exact best-response certificates. Degenerate inputs must be flagged for a separate full-set treatment.
source_locator: von Stengel Section 2, Definition 2, Propositions 1 and 3, Algorithm 4; Section 7
status_basis: The opened author survey gives support enumeration and explains its nondegeneracy requirement. The <=3 restriction is a curator-selected calibration scope.
plain_summary: Find every pair of mixed strategies that are best responses to one another in a small, fully specified mathematical game. The task tests complete case coverage and detection of inputs outside the algorithm scope; it makes no dynamical-stability claim.
assumptions: Two players, simultaneous finite normal-form game and expected-utility maximization.
Independent mixed strategies and rational payoff matrices of dimensions at most 3 by 3.

Nondegeneracy: for either player, every mixed strategy with support size k gives the opponent at most k pure best responses. Certify this over all mixed strategies, not merely equilibria or sampled points.
The task concerns equilibria of the stated game, not predictions about actual people.
scope: Nondegenerate rational bimatrix games only. Initial example: the source's equation (3), A=[[3,3],[2,5],[0,6]], B=[[3,2],[2,4],[3,0]]. Use degenerate examples only to check that the method identifies inputs outside its assumptions, not to claim the same enumeration algorithm is complete there.
target: All equilibria with exact support and best-response certificates plus an explanation of completeness under nondegeneracy.
success_criteria: Document rational input and prove or independently certify the required nondegeneracy condition.
Enumerate support pairs and retain exact feasibility decisions.
Check nonnegativity, unit sums, on-support equality and off-support payoff inequalities.
Compare with the known source example while retaining the independent completeness argument.
Route degenerate cases to a separate set-valued method; do not silently omit continua or unequal-support cases.
known_results: Von Stengel Proposition 1 characterizes best responses by support and maximum payoff.
Algorithm 4 enumerates all equilibria for a nondegenerate game; later sections describe degeneracy and full equilibrium sets.
prerequisites: Combinatorics of supports and the precise definition of nondegeneracy.
significance: A compact calibration for exhaustive reasoning, exact certificates and assumption handling. Larger market or mechanism models would need different inputs and substantive economic justification.

requirements.experiment: None for equilibrium computation. Behavioral interpretation requires a separate empirical study.
requirements.data: Only declared payoff matrices; no personal, market or experimental data are needed.
requirements.compute: At most 3 by 3 matrices with a declared bit-length bound to be set in the trial. Small support enumeration is a plausible local workload; no time, cost or success measurements exist.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Finite complete-information normal-form game; risk-neutral expected utility as represented by supplied payoffs; nondegeneracy for the selected algorithm.

ai_assessment.rationale: A finite support search and exact certificates permit independent checking. The source's fully specified example makes the trial transferable without inventing new economic claims.

clarity.reason: Inputs, outputs and equilibrium inequalities are explicit.

decomposability.reason: Check hypotheses, enumerate supports, solve, validate and prove completeness separately.

methods.reason: An opened author survey supplies definitions, algorithm and example.

search_or_symbolic.reason: Finite enumeration and rational linear algebra are directly applicable.

checkability.reason: Every candidate can be verified using payoff inequalities.

expertise.reason: Game-theory review is needed for nondegeneracy and completeness, not just algebra.

significance.reason: Valuable correctness calibration; no novel equilibrium result or behavioral prediction.

verification_difficulty.reason: Checking one equilibrium is simple; certifying the whole list and rejecting degenerate inputs is harder.

ai_assessment.uncertainty: No named model or solver was run. Reproducing familiar examples may reflect memorization. General bimatrix complexity cannot be inferred from the small trial.
ai_assessment.model_scope: No named model evaluated; assumes tool-using AI with literature retrieval, exact algebra or rational linear algebra, code generation, and access to a human domain reviewer.

obstacles: Solving indifference equations but forgetting profitable off-support deviations.
Returning one equilibrium when all were requested.
Floating-point tolerances hide zero probabilities or ties.
Mistaking a model equilibrium for a descriptive or normative recommendation.

steps: Freeze payoff orientation and all rational entries.
Certify nondegeneracy with a complete method appropriate to the small game.
Check every support case and every reported rational certificate using independently written checks.
Compare the example with the source while auditing omitted cases.
Have a reviewer inspect completeness and economic scope separately.
validation.human_review_difficulty: Moderate: arithmetic can be automated, but a game theorist should confirm hypothesis certification and all-equilibria completeness.
validation.statement_alignment: An exact best-response certificate validates the listed pair. Completeness needs the enumeration theorem and its nondegeneracy hypothesis; checking pairs alone is insufficient.

known_attempts: Von Stengel (2021) Section 2 contains an explicit worked 3 by 2 example. This literature reproduction is not a project experiment.
unresolved_checks: Set an input numerator/denominator bit-length bound before benchmarking resource use.
Select and review the independent nondegeneracy check.
A future extension to degenerate games must represent equilibrium continua and cite the relevant full-set method.
